purpose: Specify Unix spawn isolation, error typing and lossless protocol backpressure.
behavior: Compares Ready capability bits with an independent pidfd probe; hostile inherited fds/signals must be cleared, with a direct std::process control showing the hostile state is real.
Checks no-close_range fallback, pipe/null stdin, merged/separate output, normal exit codes and signal exits.
Requires typed failures for missing/nonexecutable program, bad cwd, relative program, NUL and Windows verbatim input while restoring the exact supervisor fd set, including repeated SCM_RIGHTS copies.
Sends 100,000 requests without reading to require writer backpressure and ordered recovery; a missing descriptor must close the channel and clean the tree, and 300 deferred exits must be delivered.
contracts: Pipe roots must report pid=pgid=sid with only descriptors 0,1,2 and an empty inherited signal mask.
dependencies: common Host/Cmd/OS roles and omni_proto framing; Linux seccomp facility controls.
failures_or_limits: Flood and exit-burst bounds assert finite test conditions rather than proving arbitrary-load throughput. None of these tests was run.

purpose: Specify Unix Stop behavior when inventory fails, recovers or lacks pidfd support.
behavior: Sets Linux descriptor limit three: List must return Ack::Error and Stop must not be confirmed while an out-of-group resistant leaf remains live.
Restores the limit and requires the pending Stop to finish, leaf death and the original descriptor table with no leak.
Denies pidfd syscalls and requires zero capability bits while session-rechecked fallback still stops other groups.
Checks a recovered graceful scan sends TERM before a long force deadline and a one-free-fd case uses the emergency reserve during pidfd identity recheck.
contracts: Incomplete inventory is not an empty inventory; graceful delivery must resume after a transient scan failure.
dependencies: common/os.rs prlimit/seccomp; host.rs protocol observations; role report/resist/group fixtures.
failures_or_limits: Linux-specific controls require descriptor-limit and seccomp facilities. The observed assertions are documentary only and do not validate the PID-check-to-kill race of the no-pidfd fallback.

purpose: Specify whole-session Unix Stop, root pinning, inventory and Release semantics.
behavior: Requires resistant leaves across process groups to share one force deadline while an unrelated sentinel survives; a polite control ends before its long grace.
After root exit, requires a zombie pin while descendants live, preserved exit status, orphan-only inventory, then reaping and immediate idempotent Stop when empty.
Checks idle-time grace and concurrent Stops using the earliest deadline, with exact PID/parent/name inventory matching the stop boundary.
Release hides the ID but retains the root pin and host-loss cleanup duty; a group-only kill control misses out-of-group leaves.
contracts: Unknown/released requests return Ack::Unknown; Go on a pipe root is OK and Resize without a terminal returns Ack::Error.
dependencies: common Host and independent OS liveness; inventory.rs and member_states.rs add failure-state cases.
failures_or_limits: These assertions target session-scoped cooperative containment; they do not assert that an adversarial setsid escape remains in the session. Timing windows and results were not executed.

purpose: Distinguish stopped, exiting and zombie-leader Unix processes from truly departed tree members.
behavior: Stops a root with SIGSTOP, forces a supervisor reaping pass using another root exit, and requires no false Exited plus continued List membership; resume and stdin EOF must yield exactly one real exit.
Repeatedly stops a resistant heavy leaf and requires the independent OS oracle to report it no longer alive when Stopped arrives.
On Linux, creates a zombie leader with a live resistant thread, verifies that precondition, requires List membership and the full 300 ms force grace before all threads die.
contracts: Stopped means a live workload is gone, not merely an unretrievable session query or zombie leader field.
dependencies: common role heavy/zleader fixtures; OS liveness inspects Linux tasks or macOS kernel state; Unix Stop implementation under test.
failures_or_limits: The macOS waitid behavior is stated as prior source context; the current review supplies no reproduction. These three cases cover selected difficult states, not all process-table races.
